_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a short illustration. 'nonstandard': forms hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.label: Present
entries.usage: Now or regularly.
entries.example: Γράφω ένα γράμμα.

entries.label: Future
entries.usage: θα + verb.
entries.example: Θα φύγω αύριο.

entries.label: Aorist
entries.usage: A finished past action.
entries.example: Έγραψα χθες.

entries.label: Imperfect
entries.usage: The ongoing or habitual past.
entries.example: Έγραφα κάθε μέρα.

entries.label: Perfect
entries.usage: έχω + form — completed with present relevance.
entries.example: Έχω γράψει το γράμμα.

entries.label: Subjunctive (να)
entries.usage: να + verb, aspect matters.
entries.example: Θέλω να φύγω.

entries.label: Imperative
entries.usage: Commands.
entries.example: Γράψε πιο δυνατά!

entries.label: Passive aorist
entries.usage: The action done to the subject, past.
entries.example: Το γράμμα γράφτηκε.

entries.label: Είμαι (to be)
entries.usage: Say what someone or something is — I am, you are, she is.
entries.example: Εγώ είμαι φοιτητής. — I am a student.

entries.label: Έχω (to have)
entries.usage: Say what you own or hold — Greek also uses it for being right.
entries.example: Εγώ έχω μια ερώτηση. — I have a question.

entries.label: Contracted verbs
entries.usage: A big group of verbs that stress the ending and have two equally good forms, αγαπάω or αγαπώ.
entries.example: Εγώ αγαπώ πολύ την ελληνική μουσική. — I love Greek music very much.

entries.label: Mediopassive (-ομαι)
entries.usage: A second set of endings for what happens to you, or what you do to yourself.
entries.example: Κάθε πρωί πλένομαι και ετοιμάζομαι για τη δουλειά. — Every morning I wash and get ready for work.

entries.label: Deponents
entries.usage: For coming, going and becoming, Greek uses the -ομαι endings even though nobody is doing anything to you — and their past forms are their own.
entries.example: Χθες ήρθα πολύ αργά στο σπίτι. — Yesterday I came home very late.

entries.point: Pluperfect & future perfect (είχα γράψει, θα έχω γράψει)
entries.label: Είχα γράψει (had done)
entries.usage: For what had already happened before something else, or what will be done by a certain time.
entries.example: Είχα ήδη φάει όταν ήρθαν οι φίλοι μου. — I had already eaten when my friends came.

entries.label: Participles
entries.usage: One word for while doing something, and one for something already done.
entries.example: Μπήκε στο δωμάτιο χαμογελώντας. — He entered the room smiling.

entries.label: Want / can / must
entries.usage: After θέλω, μπορώ and πρέπει comes να and a second verb that still changes with the person.
entries.example: Θέλω να φύγω νωρίς σήμερα. — I want to leave early today.

entries.label: Negation
entries.usage: Put δεν directly in front of the verb to say you don't.
entries.example: Εγώ δεν μιλάω αγγλικά. — I don't speak English.

entries.point: Υπάρχει / υπάρχουν — there is, there are
entries.label: There is / are
entries.usage: Saying something exists — one word for a single thing, another for several.
entries.example: Υπάρχει ένα βιβλίο στο τραπέζι. — There is a book on the table.

entries.label: Real conditionals
entries.usage: For an if that really might happen; the other half then says what follows — with θα, or as a command.
entries.example: Αν έχεις χρόνο, έλα να με δεις. — If you have time, come and see me.

entries.label: Unreal conditionals
entries.usage: For an if that is not true — both halves of the sentence go into the past.
entries.example: Αν ήμουν πλούσιος, θα ταξίδευα σε όλο τον κόσμο. — If I were rich, I would travel all over the world.

entries.label: Reported speech
entries.usage: Telling what someone said with ότι, or what they asked you to do with να.
entries.example: Μου είπε ότι θα αργήσει λίγο. — He told me that he'll be a bit late.

entries.point: Subordinating connectors (επειδή, ενώ, αν και, ώστε)
entries.label: Connectors
entries.usage: Joining the halves of a longer sentence: because, while, although, so that.
entries.example: Δεν ήρθα επειδή ήμουν άρρωστος. — I didn't come because I was ill.

entries.label: Accusative
entries.usage: The direct object.
entries.example: Βλέπω τον άντρα.

entries.label: Genitive
entries.usage: Possession: of.
entries.example: το βιβλίο του παιδιού

entries.point: Plural of nouns (οι φίλοι, οι πόρτες, τα βιβλία)
entries.label: Plural
entries.usage: Noun plural forms.
entries.example: ο φίλος → οι φίλοι

entries.label: Adjectives
entries.usage: Adjectives match gender, number, case.
entries.example: καλός άντρας, καλή μέρα

entries.label: Definite article
entries.usage: ο/η/το decline by case.
entries.example: ο άντρας, τον άντρα

entries.label: Gender & number
entries.usage: Every noun is a he, a she or an it, and its ending tells you which — and how many.
entries.example: Έχω δύο βιβλία. — I have two books.

entries.label: Indefinite article
entries.usage: The word for a — ένας, μία or ένα, picked to match the noun.
entries.example: Είναι μία ωραία μέρα. — It is a beautiful day.

entries.label: Subject pronouns
entries.usage: The words for I, you and they — said only when you want to stress who.
entries.example: Εγώ είμαι από την Αθήνα. — I am from Athens.

entries.label: Object pronouns
entries.usage: The short word that stands in for something already mentioned, and sits just before the verb.
entries.example: Ξέρω τον Γιώργο· τον βλέπω κάθε μέρα. — I know George; I see him every day.

entries.label: Possessives
entries.usage: The little word placed after the noun to say whose it is.
entries.example: Το αυτοκίνητό μου είναι καινούριο. — My car is new.

entries.label: Demonstratives
entries.usage: Pointing at something near or far — and Greek keeps the word for the as well.
entries.example: Αυτό το βιβλίο είναι πολύ καλό. — This book is very good.

entries.label: One-word comparatives
entries.usage: Single words for bigger, better and worse, used instead of πιο.
entries.example: Αυτό το εστιατόριο είναι καλύτερο από το άλλο. — This restaurant is better than the other one.

entries.label: Question words
entries.usage: Where, what, when, who, how, why — and the Greek question mark looks like a semicolon.
entries.example: Πού μένεις; — Where do you live?

entries.label: Prepositions
entries.usage: Small words like in, from, with and for; σε usually merges into στο and στη.
entries.example: Μένω σε μια μικρή πόλη. — I live in a small town.

entries.label: Comparison (πιο)
entries.usage: Put πιο before a describing word for more, and add the word for the to get the most.
entries.example: Η Αθήνα είναι πιο μεγάλη από τη Θεσσαλονίκη. — Athens is bigger than Thessaloniki.

entries.label: Two pronouns at once (μου το)
entries.usage: To say he gave it to me, both short words come before the verb in a fixed order.
entries.example: Το βιβλίο; Ο Γιάννης μου το έδωσε χθες. — The book? John gave it to me yesterday.

entries.label: Relative που
entries.usage: Sticking two sentences together with who, which or that — που does all three and never changes; ο οποίος is the formal alternative and does change to match the noun.
entries.example: Ο άντρας που ήρθε είναι γιατρός. — The man who came is a doctor.

entries.point: Emphasis & clitic doubling (τον Γιάννη τον ξέρω)
entries.label: Clitic doubling
entries.usage: Move what you are talking about to the front, then repeat it with a short word on the verb.
entries.example: Τον Γιάννη τον ξέρω από παιδί. — John, I've known him since childhood.

entries.label: Register
entries.usage: When you need to sound official — a notice, a form, a speech — Greek reaches for older words and set phrases instead of the everyday ones.
entries.example: Εν πάση περιπτώσει, θα τα πούμε αύριο. — In any case, we'll talk tomorrow.
